newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra raises human rights in Vietnam meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canberra raises human rights in Vietnam meeting.

text.p: Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer raised concerns about human rights with his Vietnamese counterpart on Monday, spokesmen for both ministers told reporters after the meeting.
"It was a substantive discussion," an Australian spokesman said after Downer's meeting with Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam. He refused to give further details.
Cam's spokesman said human rights were not a major point of the discussion and the dialogue on the subject had been smooth.
"(Human rights) was discussed on the basis of mutual respect of independence and national sovereignty," he said, adding that Vietnam was always prepared to discuss the subject on that basis.
Downer and Cam clashed two years ago when Downer was foreign affairs spokesman for the then Liberal-National opposition.
Downer then said he had raised human rights in discussions with Cam but the Vietnamese minister said the subject had not come up.
Australia and Vietnam clashed in 1994 and 1995 over the membership of a parliamentary delegation that Canberra wanted to send to Hanoi to discuss human rights.
The delegation was first cancelled, then revived and rescheduled but only on Hanoi's condition it not seek to intervene in Vietnamese internal affairs.
The spokesmen said on Monday that Cam and Downer had also discussed some commercial interests and furthering Australia's regional role.
Cam is in Australia for a three-day visit.
He will meet Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday.
